\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{যথেষ্ট} (jôtheshṭô)}{যথেষ্ট (jôtheshṭô)}]{\bn{যথেষ্ট} (jôtheshṭô) — enough; plenty}

\label{lesson:BN-C371-jotheshto}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for less, then the Bengali for a bit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{যথেষ্ট}}
\textbf{\bn{যথেষ্ট}} — \emph{jôtheshṭô} — \textquotedblleft{}enough; plenty\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{যথেষ্ট} \bn{টাকা} \bn{থাকলে} \bn{আমরা} \bn{নতুন} \bn{বাড়ি} \bn{কিনব।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jôtheshṭô ṭākā thākle āmrā nôtun bāṛi kinbô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If we have enough money, we'll buy a new house.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{যথেষ্ট}} (\emph{jôtheshṭô}) is Sanskrit \emph{yatheṣṭa}, 'as much as one wishes' (Monier-Williams). Bengali turned it into plain 'enough'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jôtheshṭô}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jôtheshṭô}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jôtheshṭô ṭākā thākle āmrā nôtun bāṛi kinbô.} — If we have enough money, we'll buy a new house.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for less, then the Bengali for a bit, then say \emph{jôtheshṭô} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{যথেষ্ট} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Enough; plenty\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{অতিরিক্ত} (ôtiriktô)}{অতিরিক্ত (ôtiriktô)}]{\bn{অতিরিক্ত} (ôtiriktô) — extra; excessive}

\label{lesson:BN-C371-otirikto}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a bit, then the Bengali for enough.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{অতিরিক্ত}}
\textbf{\bn{অতিরিক্ত}} — \emph{ôtiriktô} — \textquotedblleft{}extra; excessive\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{অতিরিক্ত} \bn{ব্যাগ} \bn{নিলে} \bn{বেশি} \bn{ভাড়া} \bn{দিতে} \bn{হবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ôtiriktô byāg nile beshi bhāṛā dite hôbe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you take an extra bag, you will have to pay a higher fare.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{অতিরিক্ত}} (\emph{ôtiriktô}) is Sanskrit \emph{atirikta}, left over as a surplus (Monier-Williams): more than is needed, extra or too much.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôtiriktô}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôtiriktô}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôtiriktô byāg nile beshi bhāṛā dite hôbe.} — If you take an extra bag, you will have to pay a higher fare.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a bit, then the Bengali for enough, then say \emph{ôtiriktô} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{অতিরিক্ত} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Extra; excessive\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{অল্প} (ôlpô)}{অল্প (ôlpô)}]{\bn{অল্প} (ôlpô) — a little; a small amount}

\label{lesson:BN-C371-olpo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for enough, then the Bengali for excessive.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{অল্প}}
\textbf{\bn{অল্প}} — \emph{ôlpô} — \textquotedblleft{}a little; a small amount\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{অল্প} \bn{নুন} \bn{দিলে} \bn{তরকারি} \bn{ভালো} \bn{হবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ôlpô nun dile tôrkāri bhālo hôbe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you add a little salt, the curry will be good.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{অল্প}} (\emph{ôlpô}) is Sanskrit \emph{alpa}, small or little (Monier-Williams). It is a little more formal than \bn{একটু} and can stand before a noun.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôlpô}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôlpô}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôlpô nun dile tôrkāri bhālo hôbe.} — If you add a little salt, the curry will be good.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for enough, then the Bengali for excessive, then say \emph{ôlpô} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{অল্প} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A little; a small amount\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{জোগানো} (jogāno)}{জোগানো (jogāno)}]{\bn{জোগানো} (jogāno) — to supply; to provide (for)}

\label{lesson:BN-C371-jogano}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for excessive, then the Bengali for a small amount.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{জোগানো}}
\textbf{\bn{জোগানো}} — \emph{jogāno} — \textquotedblleft{}to supply; to provide (for)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{সরকার} \bn{টাকা} \bn{জোগালে} \bn{নতুন} \bn{স্কুল} \bn{হবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sôrkār ṭākā jogāle nôtun skul hôbe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the government provides the money, there will be a new school.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{সবার} \bn{খাবার} \bn{জোগালেন}, \emph{tini sôbār khābār jogālen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{জোগানো}} (\emph{jogāno}) is listed by CDIAL 10529 (\emph{yōgy\'{\={a}}}) as Bengali jogāna, 'to supply': to fit out what is needed.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jogāno}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jogāno}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sôrkār ṭākā jogāle nôtun skul hôbe.} — If the government provides the money, there will be a new school.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for excessive, then the Bengali for a small amount, then say \emph{jogāno} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{জোগানো} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To supply; to provide (for)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{সীমা} (sīmā)}{সীমা (sīmā)}]{\bn{সীমা} (sīmā) — a limit; a boundary}

\label{lesson:BN-C371-sima}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a small amount, then the Bengali for to supply.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{সীমা}}
\textbf{\bn{সীমা}} — \emph{sīmā} — \textquotedblleft{}a limit; a boundary\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{খরচ} \bn{সীমার} \bn{বেশি} \bn{হলে} \bn{আমরা} \bn{কাজটা} \bn{বন্ধ} \bn{করব।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{khôrôch sīmār beshi hôle āmrā kājṭā bôndhô kôrbô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the cost goes over the limit, we'll stop the work.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{সীমা}} (\emph{sīmā}) is Sanskrit \emph{sīmā}, a boundary (Monier-Williams). It is the border of a field and any limit not to be passed.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sīmā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sīmā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khôrôch sīmār beshi hôle āmrā kājṭā bôndhô kôrbô.} — If the cost goes over the limit, we'll stop the work.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a small amount, then the Bengali for to supply, then say \emph{sīmā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{সীমা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A limit; a boundary\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
